titleJa: なんじから なんじまで
titleEn: From what time to what time?
summaryEn: Tell the time, ask opening hours and closed days, and talk about your daily routine: getting up, working, resting, yesterday and today.

grammar.meaningEn: Polite verb: habit or future, and its negative
grammar.exampleJa: どようびは はたらきません。
きのう やすみました。はたらきませんでした。
grammar.exampleEn: I rested yesterday. I didn't work.

grammar.meaningEn: Do something at a clock time / on a day (に); not after きのう, まいあさ, いま
grammar.exampleJa: まいあさ 6じはんに おきます。
grammar.exampleEn: I get up at 6:30 every morning.

grammar.meaningEn: From N1 until N2 (either half can stand alone)
grammar.exampleJa: びじゅつかんは 9じはんから 5じまでです。
grammar.exampleEn: The museum is open from 9:30 to 5:00.

grammar.exampleJa: やすみは どようびと にちようびです。
grammar.exampleEn: My days off are Saturday and Sunday.

grammar.meaningEn: Sentence-final ね: confirming what you heard, or showing sympathy
grammar.exampleJa: 5じまでですね。／たいへんですね。
grammar.exampleEn: Until 5, right? / That must be hard.

grammar.pattern: なんじ／なんようび／なんばん
grammar.meaningEn: What time / which day of the week / what number
grammar.exampleJa: やすみは なんようびですか。

vocab.en: your place, your side (on the phone)

tipsEn: Many Japanese museums close on Mondays. It is worth a quick call or a look at the sign before you go.
On the phone, repeat times and numbers back with ～ですね. Everyone does it, and it catches mistakes.
Careful with 4時 (よじ), 7時 (しちじ) and 9時 (くじ). Minutes switch between ふん and ぷん: 5ふん, 10ぷん.

research.notesEn: Lesson 4 introduces clock time (いま ～じ ～ふんです), the first verbs in ます form with all four polite endings (ます, ません, ました, ませんでした), time + に, から／まで, と joining nouns, sentence-final ね, and the question words なんじ, なんようび and なんばん. The only verbs are おきます, ねます, はたらきます, やすみます, べんきょうします and おわります, so scenes stay with schedules and routines. Real situations: phoning a museum, bank or library about hours and closed days, reading an opening-hours sign, and small talk about when you get up, work and rest. Typical slips: よじ／しちじ／くじ, ふん vs ぷん, adding に after きのう or まいあさ, dropping に after a clock time, saying ませんました for ませんでした, and using ます for something that happened yesterday.
